claims.text: Cr39Co18Fe18Ni18Al7 is initially in a high-temperature BCC state.
Phase stability during cooling and thermal exposure is governed by competition between chemical ordering tendencies and lattice-distortion effects.
Cooling rate influences chemical ordering and lattice-distortion effects in this alloy.
Thermal-exposure temperature influences chemical ordering and lattice-distortion effects in this alloy.
Atomic size mismatch produces lattice distortion in Cr39Co18Fe18Ni18Al7.
Suppression of atomic diffusion prevents chemical ordering.
Preventing chemical ordering favors retention of a disordered BCC phase.
Slow cooling and annealing permit sufficient atomic diffusion for chemical ordering.
Chemical ordering can produce B2 or L21 ordered phases.
Lattice distortion can stabilize or destabilize ordered phases depending on thermal-exposure temperature.
Quenching at greater than 100 K/s should yield a predominantly disordered BCC phase.
Slow cooling at less than 1 K/s followed by annealing between approximately 500°C and 700°C for 24 hours should promote B2 or L21 formation relative to the unannealed rapidly cooled baseline.
Annealing above approximately 700°C may destabilize the ordered phases because lattice-distortion effects increase.
A rapidly cooled, unannealed sample is expected to retain a disordered BCC phase.
The proposed mechanism should also apply to similar high-entropy alloys having significant atomic-size mismatch and chemical-ordering tendencies.
The proposed mechanism may not apply to alloys with negligible atomic-size mismatch or weak chemical-ordering tendencies.
